text:
Morgan: FYI customer (FinData) asks for a Private deployment POC. They want minimal internet egress, strict firewall rules, and a way to route from their app VPC into Redwood without public IPs. What's our recommended pattern for AWS? VPC peering vs PrivateLink vs Transit GW?
Priya: short answer: PrivateLink (AWS PrivateLink / interface endpoints) for private API access from customer VPC is simplest for one-to-one connectivity. Transit Gateway if they need hub-and-spoke across multiple VPCs. VPC peering works but has no transitive routing and requires route table changes.
Sam: @Priya can you confirm expected ports and the IP range we need to allow in their firewall? Security team will only allow ranges they can justify in docs.
Alex: We usually expose an NLB-backed AWS PrivateLink endpoint for Redwood Private. Customer opens outbound connection to the endpoint ENIs in their VPC (so traffic stays in AWS network). Ports: TLS/443 for API; if they're using mTLS or a custom ingress, we'll call that out. No additional ports by default.
Ryan: A couple of notes:
- For PrivateLink (interface endpoint) we publish a service name; customer creates the endpoint in their VPC and traffic flows to our NLB.
- ENI IPs are in the customer's VPC; they control SGs. Recommend SG ingress: allow TCP 443 from the app CIDR only.
- If they want to restrict to specific IPs, we give them the service VPC endpoint DNS names rather than fixed IPs (the ENIs can change).
Priya: For the POC checklist:
- Confirm AWS account IDs and preferred region(s)
- Customer creates interface endpoint in their VPC pointing to our service name
- Customer updates ACLs / SGs to allow outbound to endpoint ENIs on 443
- Share sample security questionnaire responses and minimal IAM requirements
- Validate latency + egress behavior in POC (we add a test harness)
Morgan: They asked about on-prem or cross-cloud scenarios (Azure). Is PrivateLink an option there?
Alex: For Azure we support Private Link equivalents via Private Endpoint + a fronting Azure Load Balancer. The pattern is similar but there is more customer-side setup (NSG rules, private DNS zone linking). If it's hybrid (on-prem -> VPC), customers often use Transit GW + VPN/DirectConnect to reach the VPC with the interface endpoint.
Sam: They also asked about pricing — any one-time setup or is there an ongoing charge for PrivateLink?
Priya: Pricing note: Private deployment (Private control plane) has a baseline infra fee per month + per-instance / reserved capacity costs. PrivateLink endpoint itself is AWS-managed billing on the customer's side (they pay AWS for the ENIs/endpoint hours and data processing). We don't charge extra specifically for PrivateLink beyond Private deployment contract, but if we have to run extra NLB capacity for them that can be included in the sizing quote. I'll echo: AWS endpoint costs are billed to the customer.
Ryan: Firewall rules we typically recommend (example for SGs):
```
Type: Outbound
Protocol: TLS (TCP 443)
Destination: interface endpoint ENI CIDR (or allow to endpoint by security group)
Description: Allow app -> Redwood PrivateLink
```
If they're using a NAT + egress-only model, they'll need to allow outbound to our public egress IPs (we can provide a minimal set for the POC) but that's only for public-hosted API. PrivateLink avoids that.
Sam: Can you paste a one-liner AWS command we can give their infra team to create the endpoint?
Alex: Sure — example (customer runs in their account):
```
aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint --vpc-id vpc-0123456789abcdef0 --service-name com.amazonaws.vpce.us-west-2.vpce-svc-xxxxxxxx --vpc-endpoint-type Interface --subnet-ids subnet-aaaa subnet-bbbb --security-group-ids sg-xxxxxx
```
Morgan: Any enterprise blockers we should flag on the security questionnaire side? They asked about audit logs, KMS, and data residency.
Priya: Callouts to include in SQ response:
- We support customer-managed KMS for Private deployments (specify KMS ARN)
- Audit logs: Console/agent exports of request/ops logs to S3 are available; can hook into their logging pipeline via S3 or syslog in private infra setups.
- Data residency: we can deploy entirely in specified region; confirm region and AZ requirements early.
Ryan: Also mention network egress path for dependency services (DNS, CRL checks). Some enterprise firewalls block outbound to Internet for CRL/OCSP; ensure they allow outbound to the CRL endpoints needed by our cert provider or use internal PKI.
Sam: They want a minimal SG example I can paste to tickets.
Priya: paste this for app->endpoint (replace CIDR/subnet ids):
```
# allow app subnet to reach PrivateLink endpoint
aws ec2 authorize-security-group-ingress --group-id sg-app --protocol tcp --port 443 --cidr 10.10.0.0/24 --description "allow app->redwood pl endpoint"
```
And endpoint SG on their side: allow ingress from app SG (by SG id) or app CIDR on 443.
Morgan: Great. Anything else for POC timeline? They want to start next week.
Alex: We can spin up the Private NLB/service side in <48h once contract/POC account details are provided. Need: account ID, vpc endpoint service region, desired availability zones. After endpoint create, we'll validate with a small load and share curl test.
infra-bot: NOTE: created tracking ticket #RDW-POC-3921 for "FinData PrivateLink POC" — assignee: Priya.
Ryan: One final nuance: VPC peering is okay for single VPC pairs but if the customer wants to peer several VPCs to a shared service VPC, Transit Gateway or PrivateLink is preferred. Also peering has no support for cross-account security groups.
Sam: Awesome, I'm sharing these steps. Can you also provide the small sample curl test?
Priya: sample: `curl -v --resolve api.redwood.example:443:10.10.12.34 https://api.redwood.example/health` — verify 200 OK and latency. We'll provide exact hostname once the endpoint is active.
Morgan: Thanks all — I'll send this to the customer and cc legal for the deployment contract. :thumbsup:
